en: Most valiant, with fierce wrath,
With a head like a small cauldron,
With brows like a recumbent camel,
uncertainty_note: The first comparison noun is difficult; нардай is the best visible reading.

en: With teeth like a whip,
uncertainty_note: The comparison word is provisional; the handwriting is indistinct.

en: His face loomed as vast as the whole world,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is slightly faint but readable in context.

en: His crown stood sharp against the rain,
uncertainty_note: Several letters in this epithet are difficult; translation is a literal completion-first rendering.

en: He had a head broad as the back of a palm,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript wording is uncertain, especially the middle noun phrase.

en: In battle his face thrust forward,
uncertainty_note: The verbal phrase is translated contextually.

en: He did not fear one who answered back,
When he merely flicked his brow,
uncertainty_note: The verb appears to be силкип but is not fully secure.

en: He laid low every foe he seized,
He made his own name mighty,
uncertainty_note: Literally “made his own head great”; rendered idiomatically.

en: When he merely knit his brow,
He disgraced them on the spot.
At his menace, men died of fright,
His visage blazed with wrath,
uncertainty_note: The last word is a provisional reading from a heavily joined hand.

en: No man could endure approaching him,
A man spoken of like a wild beast,
uncertainty_note: The line is difficult; Кайберен and the following wording are provisional.

en: Such a man stood there.
His executioners numbered seven hundred,
He had four thousand nobles,
His guards had their appointed fortune,
uncertainty_note: The noun phrase after Кароолчулар is difficult and this translation is provisional.

en: They stood with swords drawn.
Guards for the treasury,
uncertainty_note: Казынкана is a provisional reading of a joined form, interpreted contextually as “for the treasury.”

en: Finishing their words, they fell silent,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is read ток эте; punctuation is editorial.

en: The short of the angry words was this,
uncertainty_note: Кыжырына and the grammatical relation are provisional because the handwriting is tightly joined.

en: The chiefs who would not disperse,
uncertainty_note: Тарамашын is a provisional reading and contextual rendering.

en: When the decree remained, he cried out,
uncertainty_note: The final verb is provisionally read какрады.

en: He had risen since the dawn,
uncertainty_note: The last word is pale and provisionally read алганы.

en: They would not tell him to turn back to his horse,
uncertainty_note: The syntax of Атына кайтар is uncertain; English follows the most plausible contextual sense.

en: They would not go and cause distress,
uncertainty_note: A clear baseline, though the precise force of азар салып is contextual.

en: Now among the Chinese of forty kinds,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is difficult and provisionally read жанрын; English is correspondingly tentative.

en: His disordered muttering,
uncertainty_note: Both words are pale; күбүргү is a provisional noun reading.

en: They would not remain to turn back with a shout.
uncertainty_note: Үкүрүк and the verbal construction are provisional.

en: Ever a khan to the enemy people,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears written Джоо/Жоо; normalized here as Жоо.

en: Murmuring in submission,
uncertainty_note: Күбүргүн is provisionally read; English interprets топу кылып idiomatically.

en: Pouring out and raking over your airs,
uncertainty_note: The final word is highly uncertain and may not be күүлөргүн.

en: Cast down beneath,
uncertainty_note: Тобонко is a provisional manuscript spelling/read for a downward direction.

en: His splendor looked like a mountain,
uncertainty_note: The initial word is provisionally read Көркөмү.

en: With arms as massive as a cart,
uncertainty_note: The phrase is read literally but its idiomatic sense is uncertain.

en: His excellence was his courage,
uncertainty_note: The first word is faint but plausibly Артыктыгы.

en: He appeared as one son of humankind.
uncertainty_note: The ending and case relation are provisional.

en: Here too were two khans,
uncertainty_note: The numeral is clear; the opening word is somewhat joined.

en: Roaring with a fearsome air,
uncertainty_note: Best-effort reading; Айбаттанып is slightly pale.

en: Of the Chinese who shook the forty tribes,
uncertainty_note: The object “tribes” is supplied in English; the Kyrgyz line only gives кырк.

en: Sending word and summoning them,
uncertainty_note: The first verb is pale but plausibly Билдирип.

en: The massed Chinese had forty khans,
uncertainty_note: The final word is cramped but appears эле.

en: Now the chosen ones of the forty clans,
uncertainty_note: The final form элеги and its interpretation as “chosen ones” are provisional.

en: The son of the forty maidens,
uncertainty_note: Кыздардын is the most plausible reading, though the medial letters are joined.

en: The gathered Chinese stood watching,
uncertainty_note: Чогуу is pale but fits the visible letters and context.

en: We were the ones who stood out,
uncertainty_note: The first word is provisional; English follows a possible sense of чочоюу.

en: Could it be in the tidings?
uncertainty_note: The line is visually fairly clear; the interrogative nuance depends on context.

en: With a horse for a six-day journey,
uncertainty_note: The first word could be алты; the reading is contextually strong.

en: With a letter the size of a palm,
uncertainty_note: Алкандай is a provisional reading, interpreted as алакандай.

en: Driving the horse through the blizzard,
uncertainty_note: The middle noun and verb are provisional; English gives the likely motion image.

en: Circling its four corners,
uncertainty_note: The first verb may be Тегеренип/Тогоронуп; the manuscript appears closest to Тогоронуп.

en: Casting his eyes all around,
uncertainty_note: The syntax is compressed; English renders the apparent directional sense.

en: You sent wanderers among the people,
uncertainty_note: The second word is a provisional reading of joined cursive; the sense may concern sending word through the people.

en: You gathered news from the people,
Here stood Ysyk-Tekur,
uncertainty_note: The final two words appear to be a proper name or title, provisionally read Ысык-Текур.

en: Was he the blue-maned gray,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript seems to read көк жалдыгы көк белем; the idiomatic force and punctuation are uncertain.

en: One grave word from Koloy,
uncertainty_note: The first name is provisionally normalized as Колой; the line is syntactically continued.

en: As though endowed with great courage,
Did the great one go striking with his sword,
uncertainty_note: The middle phrase is difficult cursive; кылыч кыйган is the best visual reading.

en: As though he went with the valiant one.
uncertainty_note: Кайран is clear, but its referent and the instrumental construction are context-dependent.

en: When the third stood here,
To continue the tale briefly,
Of the Chinese, of distant Kakan,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is provisionally read аркы.

en: He gathered its teeming people,
When Suurman stood there,
uncertainty_note: The apparent proper name Суурманын may instead be an inflected common noun or another name.

en: There was no one to turn them back,
uncertainty_note: The phrase кай кайтарлар is a best-effort reading of compressed cursive.

en: His treasury remained unbroken,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase looks like бузуу жок; English gives its likely contextual sense.

en: When he took the reckoning,
There was no city besides Kakan,
When the teeming Chinese remained,
Third, to Dyisha,
uncertainty_note: The case endings and the proper name Дыйша are clear enough visually, but the compressed syntax depends on the next lines.

en: His son, the city’s herald,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read бакырчун and interpreted as one who cries out or proclaims.

en: The khan’s night had fallen,
uncertainty_note: The line appears to read түндү калганы, but its precise idiomatic sense is uncertain.

en: There was no one at all to guard the frontier,
uncertainty_note: Каш кайтарлар is a provisional reading; каш may refer to an edge or frontier.

en: Look closely: this people is Beijing,
uncertainty_note: The opening imperative is provisionally read Бейлеп көр.

en: Koloy’s grim, dark might,
uncertainty_note: The name Колой and the intensifying phrase кор кара are best-effort readings.

en: This black host belongs to Dyisha,
uncertainty_note: The final proper name and possessive ending are provisionally read Дыйшанын.

en: He has a people swarming like black worms,
All the people of forty tribes are there,
The elder of all the people,
The ablest of the spearmen,
uncertainty_note: The last word is provisionally read ыктуусу.

en: The finest of those who mount the troop,
uncertainty_note: Топ мингендин is visually likely, though the expression may carry a specialized martial sense.

en: This is the pasha of Beijing,
The tent of the watchman,
uncertainty_note: The first word appears to be Кароолчунун; its relation to the surrounding epithets is uncertain.

en: The hero of the people of Kakan,
Together with Suurulma and Chyng Tengir,
uncertainty_note: Суурулма is a provisional manuscript reading; the printed counterpart has Суурулган.

en: There are two heroes who win the horses,
uncertainty_note: The joined middle word is read утканы; sense remains provisional.

en: Their names resound among the people,
uncertainty_note: The handwriting is difficult; raw reading and contextual translation are provisional.

en: They are a blessing to us,
There is a pair of heroes,
While the two of us stand here,
Would some grim mighty foe confront us?
uncertainty_note: The phrase суук зор is visually plausible but may contain a personal or ethnic name.

en: Would one who has gone as an equal strike us?
uncertainty_note: The line is difficult and its idiomatic sense is uncertain.

en: Could an enemy break the heroes?
uncertainty_note: The final verb is read бузабы; the printed counterpart differs.

en: Would a man turn back without dying?
The old man Zhangju, the messenger,
No such soul comes from ordinary men,
Traveling alone, he had seen the lands,
Riding alone, he had seen the peoples,
Who made Ala-Too his homeland,
The people called him their enemy,
uncertainty_note: The first word may be Ага; syntax is provisional.

en: No living soul had defeated his might,
uncertainty_note: Алымын is a provisional reading and is translated contextually as might.

en: The lineage of two daughters,
uncertainty_note: The final word appears укуму, probably a nonstandard or reduced form of тукуму.

en: A descendant of brave Kökchö,
His thought of the enemy was keen,
uncertainty_note: The compact noun phrase admits more than one interpretation.

en: Of these scattered Burut people,
uncertainty_note: аңтарылган and буруктун are provisional readings; бурут is interpreted as the ethnonym.

en: Look at the descendant who remained,
They say Akjoltoy and Seytek have died,
To the true abode from which none return,
They say both died and beheld it,
They say they set out upon that journey,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript reading and the idiomatic force of тартып are provisional.

en: This fleeting world of seven days,
They say its course is sorrow,
uncertainty_note: The first two words are difficult and the English gives the likely contextual sense.

en: The person who goes does not return,
He has entered the dark grave,
Word passes down from sage to sage,
A descendant remained from Seytek,
The finest of them, a young champion,
uncertainty_note: The first phrase is read Эң коозу, but the handwriting is faint and may instead name the youngest descendant.

en: From the great branch that would remain with Kerimche,
uncertainty_note: The opening proper name and the verb are difficult; provisionally read Керимче калыр.

en: I heard that no offspring remained,
uncertainty_note: The first word is written Укум, likely a reduced spelling of тукум; the polarity of калба is retained.

en: Among peoples of many different ranks,
uncertainty_note: The opening word is provisionally read Төрү.

en: One named Kenen was born,
I heard that a descendant remained.
Making Ala-Too his homeland,
I heard that Kongur remained,
uncertainty_note: Коңур may be a personal name or an abbreviated reference to Kongurbay.

en: When he went to Karakuman,
uncertainty_note: The place name is provisionally read Каракуман.

en: When Kaltai attacked from his side,
uncertainty_note: Калтай is treated as a proper name; the idiom жагынан салганда is translated contextually.

en: Fleeing, he saved the khan alive,
uncertainty_note: The first word and the phrase соо кылып are visually plausible; the object may instead be канын “his blood.”

en: Laying a claim against Kaltai,
uncertainty_note: The proper name and idiomatic force of доо кылып remain provisional.

en: I heard that he took his blood in vengeance.
uncertainty_note: Канын алды is clear enough visually but may mean either killed him or avenged blood.

en: Advancing three times from the right flank,
uncertainty_note: The numeral and final participle are difficult; read provisionally as үч жүрүп.

en: They say he waged a boundless battle,
uncertainty_note: The first word is provisionally read Опсуз.

en: Standing face to face,
Firing muskets and drawing bows,
They fought in a bloody clash,
Firing the great jazayil and the bow,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to read Жазайыл чоң; punctuation and syntax are uncertain.

en: They say the wretched Kyrgyz attacked.
uncertainty_note: The middle ethnonym is read кыргыз, though the handwriting is compressed.

en: The Örötkül came and moved around them,
uncertainty_note: Өрөткүл is treated as a group or proper name; the last phrase is difficult.

en: The Chinese who went unpunished,
uncertainty_note: The first word is provisionally read Жазасыз.

en: Ambushing them in a hidden place and striking them down,
uncertainty_note: Буйткада and the martial sense of жайлап чаптырып are contextual readings.

en: Scattering all their possessions,
The Örötkül then turned back.
uncertainty_note: The group or proper name is provisionally read Өрөткүл.

en: Turning back the edge of that host,
Their hero was Badykan,
uncertainty_note: The proper name is provisionally read Бадыкан.

en: That glaring Chinese warrior,
uncertainty_note: The final word is read кытай; the short line may be syntactically attached to its neighbors.

en: With no soul left to answer back,
That ill-fated eagle,
uncertainty_note: The epithet is provisionally read Кара жолтой.

en: Casting them down as though slaughtered,
uncertainty_note: The phrase is provisionally read Кырган сындай.

en: Without looking any man in the face,
uncertainty_note: The final form is manuscript-like каралбай, whose syntax is irregular.

en: Black-headed and fork-footed,
Unable to reckon a man worth even coarse cloth,
uncertainty_note: The line is difficult; жоон бөзгө is visually likely and the English is contextual.

en: Having every passerby bound,
uncertainty_note: The first word is provisionally read Каттаганды.

en: Bringing down the leopard-like khan.
uncertainty_note: The manuscript seems to read кабылан канын; the syntax may instead refer to “leopard blood.”

en: From the man who went to meet them,
uncertainty_note: The first word is read Каршы; the clause continues from the preceding folio.

en: He has wrung the news from him.
uncertainty_note: The joined manuscript reading Кабаргасын соолуттур and its translation are provisional.

en: His heroism and princely bearing,
uncertainty_note: The second noun is read шаазылыгын; spelling and nuance are uncertain.

en: He is a warrior better than them all,
A man who traveled there has seen him,
uncertainty_note: Каттап is a best-effort reading of the first word.

en: To every eye that beholds him, he is wondrous,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript is faint and crowded; баары укмуштур is reconstructed provisionally from the visible letterforms and sense.

en: He roamed among peoples and reconnoitered lands,
uncertainty_note: The line is read contextually; the final word is cramped.

en: The riders who went to gather news
Lost their wits,
Saddling their horses and making ready,
uncertainty_note: The middle phrase is a difficult manuscript reading, provisionally normalized as ат-так куруп.

en: The hero, a moon-bright eagle,
uncertainty_note: This entire short line is a provisional reading; the hand is heavily joined.

en: Set out at that very time.
Making camp at a lodging place,
Taking the spoils that lay spread out,
uncertainty_note: The final phrase is read олжор алып; morphology and translation remain uncertain.

en: His countless treasuries were filled,
The damned Kyrgyz people
Had returned and settled in their encampment.
Making Ala-Too their homeland,
And making that Kenen their hero,
Yielding no ground when surrounded,
uncertainty_note: The first word is read Курчоого; this manuscript-only line has no direct printed counterpart.

en: Submitting to no man of courage,
They settled in Talas as their land.
uncertainty_note: The compressed middle verb is read жердеп.

en: If we make a nest for the shamed,
uncertainty_note: Both manuscript reading and idiomatic force are provisional.

en: If we ask among the hills,
uncertainty_note: The first word is read Адырлардан; the line may preserve a proper name or variant form.

en: His forefather was the hero Khan Manas,
His grandfather was Semetey,
His own father was the hero Seytek,
Of all of those men,
He fell short of them not by a hair,
He grew like a mighty plane tree,
He guarded all his borderlands,
He had drawn close to the Chinese,
uncertainty_note: A clear manuscript variant absent from the nearby printed run; салыптыр is certain but the idiom is contextual.

en: Red gold and white silver coins,
uncertainty_note: The final noun is read дилде, a coin-name; the handwriting is faint.

en: All that ears have heard and eyes have seen,
Saying he would seize it from the land,
uncertainty_note: Translation is provisional because the line continues syntactically.

en: Flaming up like a white gale,
uncertainty_note: The final line is faint; read Ак шамалдай шамданып and continues on the next folio.

en: Grieving, he would close his eyes,
uncertainty_note: The first word and the future-form final verb are provisional; the line continues the preceding folio.

en: Those who pursued him pressed onward,
uncertainty_note: The first word is difficult and provisionally read Өккөндөр; translation follows that reading.

en: Softening that people,
uncertainty_note: The opening particle and verb are faint; read provisionally as Оо жибитип.

en: They say he found it as he had hoped,
Coming thoughtfully to the barren shore,
uncertainty_note: The phrase как жака is a literal best-effort reading whose idiomatic force is uncertain.

en: They say he found what lay at the root of his thought.
uncertainty_note: The joined middle wording is provisionally segmented as Ой түп жүргөн.

en: Like Manas, over Afghanistan,
uncertainty_note: Манасындай and Оогандын are the best visual readings; syntax continues into the following lines.

en: He crushed its turmoil,
uncertainty_note: The first noun is provisionally read Тоболонун and may be a different inflected form.

en: He scattered its four kinds of livestock,
Binding its claim through hunger,
uncertainty_note: Both the source segmentation and translation are provisional.

en: Entering from Karak toward its mountain,
uncertainty_note: Карактан may be a place-name or a different noun; кире тоосун is also uncertain.

en: Tethering his mares on its pasture,
uncertainty_note: The faint line is read Өрүшүнө тигип бээсин from the visible letterforms and context.

en: He bore down upon them from above,
uncertainty_note: Тобосунан is a provisional reading; the idiom is translated contextually.

en: He crushed their nobles,
Taking the booty and that people he found,
uncertainty_note: олжон may preserve a manuscript case-form or a different word; punctuation and syntax are provisional.

en: He subdued the four who had found shelter,
uncertainty_note: The entire short line is difficult; Төрт сыйган is a best-effort reading.

en: He scattered their four kinds of livestock,
The Afghan domain he had set his mind upon,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read оосун; translation follows the surrounding Afghanistan episode.

en: Without turning the reins toward the seat of honor,
uncertainty_note: The verb is read кыйбастан but could be a closely written alternative.

en: There, standing exposed, their spirit broke,
uncertainty_note: Калкайда and the possessive force of жини are contextually interpreted.

en: He turned back the Afghan herds.
uncertainty_note: The final verb appears буруптур; its object relation is contextual.

en: At that time, that people,
Saying the gray wolf had moved them away,
uncertainty_note: The first word is read Көчүрүп and кокжал is clear; syntax and subject remain provisional.

en: Turned every one of their necks.
uncertainty_note: The opening word is provisionally read Калайы and may encode another form.

en: A small number of Muslims,
uncertainty_note: The comparative-looking form ганадай is faint; sense is provisional.

en: Saying, “I shall make it a shrine,”
uncertainty_note: Мазар is the contextual reading of a lightly written word that resembles мезер.

en: Having once been born into the world,
Saying he had come upon the face of the earth,
Making his court in Kokand,
Making that one into a shrine,
uncertainty_note: The first word again resembles мезер but is normalized provisionally as мазар.

en: He set it close to paradise,
uncertainty_note: таяуу is retained as written; the exact idiom is provisional.

en: Losing sight of the white yurts,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read жаздан; translation treats көз жаз- as the idiom “lose sight of.”

en: Taking Afghanistan and Konguz,
uncertainty_note: The final word is difficult and provisionally treated as the place-name Коңуз.

en: Making that one a saint,
He laid out his paradise wide.
uncertainty_note: The middle adjective is read кең; the possessive and idiomatic translation are provisional.

en: Gathering around a corrupt man,
uncertainty_note: The second half is read адамга түйүлүп; the exact idiomatic force is provisional.

en: Whatever ears had heard and eyes had seen,
uncertainty_note: Clear; punctuation supplied.

en: All the people called it an inheritance,
uncertainty_note: Clear; мураа is the manuscript spelling of мурас.

en: They had taken it as their pretext,
uncertainty_note: Clear; contextual translation of баана.

en: That people took the good-for-nothing,
uncertainty_note: The line is clear but its sentence continues into the next baseline.

en: And made him their champion.
uncertainty_note: Clear; караан has the contextual sense of a person relied upon.

en: Of distant Khodynch,
uncertainty_note: The place or people name is difficult and provisionally read Ходынчтын.

en: The finest of the Khakanians was its khan,
uncertainty_note: The long baseline is faint; Каканчынын and the syntax are provisional.

en: Among the Chinese people of forty khans,
uncertainty_note: Clear apart from whether хан qualifies эл collectively.

en: There were a thousand watchful eyes,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript appears to read Миң көздөрүн молу экен; grammar and meaning are uncertain.

en: There was a gray-maned hero to rule the people,
uncertainty_note: The final words are provisionally read бару экен.

en: To all of Khodynch,
uncertainty_note: The proper name is provisionally read Ходынч.

en: Sending word by a written notice,
uncertainty_note: The first compound is read Кулак кагаз; its precise sense is uncertain.

en: The nobles Ebei and Shygai,
uncertainty_note: The two names and улугу are reasonably visible but may be variant names.

en: He set the Kazakhs marching against the Khakan,
uncertainty_note: The verb and object are difficult; provisionally read Каканга казак баштаттыр.

en: Every living soul gathered,
uncertainty_note: The opening word is faint but appears to be Ар.

en: The Chinese who had drawn their swords,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript form is read Кылычын керген; possibly a different verb.

en: The Chinese people of forty khans,
uncertainty_note: Clear; the genitive leads into the following baseline.

en: Gathered in Beijing,
uncertainty_note: The place name and verb are clear.

en: In this Beijing upon which radiance poured,
uncertainty_note: The middle word is read төгүлгөн; slightly faint.

en: In this inexhaustible land,
uncertainty_note: The adjective is provisionally read түгөнгүс.

en: There then stood the Old Khan,
uncertainty_note: The name or epithet Кары хан is clear.

en: Before the eyes of the Old Khan,
uncertainty_note: The case ending on хандын is faint but the reading fits the visible text.

en: The one who became khan over ten khans,
uncertainty_note: The syntax may instead continue a count into the next line.

en: When two thousand years had been fulfilled,
uncertainty_note: The numeral appears to read Эки миң, though this extraordinary age may be formulaic.

en: The Old Khan lived long,
uncertainty_note: Clear.

en: When he was among the people,
uncertainty_note: Clear words; contextual subject supplied in English.

en: Born in Altai and grown mighty,
uncertainty_note: The place name is read Алтайда; the first letter is faint.

en: His people gazed their fill at him, moonlike,
uncertainty_note: The manuscript reading Айдайын журту тойгон and its idiom are uncertain.

en: They saw no defect in his stature,
uncertainty_note: The line is faint and provisionally read Боюнун кемин көрүптүр.

en: He became a match for foreign peoples,
uncertainty_note: The postposition is provisionally read -ка and чак as “a match.”

en: His spoken word brought contentment,
uncertainty_note: The last word is faint and provisionally read канаат.

en: The forty tribes of China, to the Khakan,
uncertainty_note: Clear overall; the sentence continues into the next baseline.

en: Paid neither tribute nor tax,
uncertainty_note: Clear.

en: And did not heed the word he spoke.
uncertainty_note: Clear; punctuation supplied.

en: Without treading the road that was laid out,
uncertainty_note: Opening verb and its relation to the following line are clear enough; exact idiom is provisional.

en: He would leave them a land of pursuit,
uncertainty_note: The faint middle and final words are provisionally read куугун жер койлот.

en: Without looking to the one who drove them,
uncertainty_note: The dative noun is pale and provisionally read Айдоочуга.

en: He would set the people fighting behind him,
uncertainty_note: The opening word and final verb are difficult; reading and translation are provisional.

en: He set fighter against fighter in combat,
